newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds gear up for FOMC relief rally.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds gear up for FOMC relief rally.

text.p: Australian bonds failed to make much more headway after an initial U.S.-led rally with the market content to sit out and wait for the outcome of the Federal Open Market Committee rather than second guess it.
A 25 basis point tightening in the Fed funds rate to 5.50 percent has been fully factored in, and such a result could prompt a relief rally on Wednesday, analysts said.

However, the Fed's statement which follows the meeting will also be heavily scrutinised for any clues for future policy adjustments. The FOMC result is expected at around 6.15 a.m. Wednesday (1915 GMT Tuesday).

Economists at Bankers Trust Australia expect the Fed to tighten by a further 25 basis points later this year to 5.75 percent, possibly in May, but do not expect this to have a lasting impact on local markets as Australia is at a different point in the cycle.

"Given Australia's relatively good inflation outlook and still high employment, the expected U.S. tightening does not change our view of no rise in official cash rates before mid-1998," said David Bassanese, senior economist at BT.
Australian official interest rates currently stand at 6.0 percent.
One local development that the market is still hanging out for is the Industrial Relation Commision's decision on the trade union's "living wage" claim, expected any time soon.
Economists expect a settlement of around A$12 per week, which is unlikely to concern the Reserve Bank in its thinking over future wage inflation, although above A$15 could set off alarm bells.

A late rally in U.S. Treasuries on Monday, triggered by a surge in U.S. stocks pre-empting a post-FOMC relief rally, provided local bonds with a firm footing and took the 10-year bond yield back below 8.0 percent.
